narrative.northStar: The Site Plan You Can Walk Into
narrative.overview:
Gold Bears is drawn, not rendered. Everything sits on warm drafting paper ruled with an ink grid, and the landing opens on a survey-true massing model of JRR Hall, built from Vexcel footprints and roof heights. The hall is solid paper-white with gold coping and a gold-framed, lit entrance. Its neighbours are ghosted ink line-work. A north arrow and a 0–30 m scale bar sit on the ground plane. Scrolling is one continuous camera move: an aerial three-quarter view, an orbit, a descent to eye height at the plaza, and a walk through the door that cross-fades into the live Matterport tour. The studio then opens in that same space.

The interface's panels, cards and bars float over the drawing as frosted glass: warm translucent panels with a white hairline edge and a soft, low, warm shadow, so the model always reads through. The typography gives the drawing its voice. Schibsted Grotesk sets heavy, tightly tracked two-tone titles (ink over deep gold). Geist carries the body text in plain words. Geist Mono handles anything that is a measurement, a step number, a status or a data credit. Gold is scarce and means one of two things: the subject (the hall's roof edge, its door, the bear mark) or a point of attention (area and pin dots, step-number badges, focus, hover, progress).

Density is generous on the landing, where panels are left-docked, at most 620px wide, with long scroll runs between them, and compact in the studio, where glass panels dock to the viewport edges at a 12px inset around a full-bleed scene.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper (#F4EFE7) with a two-scale ink drafting grid, in both CSS and the 3D ground plane.
A survey-true massing model as the hero subject, credited in a mono caption.
In 3D, line weight is carried by opacity, not stroke width.
Frosted glass over a live scene for every panel, card and bar.
Two-tone display titles: an ink line, then a deep-gold sub-line.
Mono for every measured or numbered fact.
Scroll as a single continuous camera move, ending in a cross-fade into the real interior.

rules.name: The Gold Is the Subject Rule
rules.body: In the scene, gold belongs only to the building you will enter: its coping strip, its door frame and its plaza mark. Neighbours never take gold. In the UI, gold marks points of attention: area and pin dots, the 16% gold badge behind plan-step numerals, and focus, hover and progress states. It is never a solid fill behind text.

rules.name: The Two Inks Rule
rules.body: UI ink (`ink`) is used opaque, on DOM text and fills. Scene ink (`scene-ink`) is used translucent, on WebGL line-work. Do not swap them.

rules.name: The Evidence Colour Rule
rules.body: Blue, amber and green say where a fact came from, or what state it is in: scan, tape or caution, verified. They appear only as tag tints (6% fill, 35% border, full-strength text), status dots and short status lines. They are never decoration.

rules.name: The Two-Tone Title Rule
rules.body: Every display and headline is two lines: a statement in ink, then a short sub-line in `sub` gold, nested in the same heading element.

rules.name: The Measured-in-Mono Rule
rules.body: Anything measured, numbered, sourced or reporting status is set in Geist Mono. This covers dimensions, step numbers, the site caption and its data credit, provenance notes, run status, and scale-bar lettering. Titles, explanatory copy and buttons are never set in mono.

rules.name: The Glass Over the Drawing Rule
rules.body: Panels, cards and bars are translucent and blurred so the model reads through them. An opaque card over the scene breaks the world. Opaque surfaces are limited to small scene annotations and to field-white wells and rows inside glass.

rules.name: The Warm Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows are tinted warm brown (rgba 40–45, 30–32, 12–15), soft, and drawn with negative spread. They are never neutral grey and never hard-edged.

dos: **Do** keep every panel, card and bar on frosted glass (`glass` fill, 20px blur, white hairline edge, warm negative-spread shadow) so the scene reads through.
**Do** write every display and headline as two lines: ink, then a `sub` gold sub-line.
**Do** set measurements, step numbers, captions, data credits, notes and status in Geist Mono at weight 400 or 500.
**Do** credit survey data in the mono site caption whenever the site model is shown.
**Do** carry 3D line hierarchy with opacity tiers (0.7 / 0.55 / 0.22 / 0.2 / 0.15) in scene ink, and build heavy emphasis as geometry.
**Do** reserve gold for the subject building in the scene, and for focus, hover, active and progress states in the UI.
**Do** use the evidence colours only to say where a fact came from (scan blue, tape amber, verified green).
**Do** give every scroll-driven move a reduced-motion path that holds the camera's azimuth and removes smoothing and parallax.
donts: **Don't** set text in `gold` (2.25:1) or `mute` (2.49:1). Use `gold-ink`, `sub` or `ink-2`.
**Don't** give neighbouring buildings gold, solid fills or strong edges. Context stays at 0.18 fill and 0.15 line opacity.
**Don't** place opaque cards over the scene. Opaque surfaces are limited to small annotation capsules and to wells and rows inside glass.
**Don't** use neutral-grey or hard offset shadows. Shadows are soft and warm-tinted.
**Don't** put a small tracked mono label above a heading as a kicker. Mono labels describe data, not sections.
**Don't** use Unicode characters as icon controls or status marks. Draw icons as inline SVG, as the scroll cue does.
**Don't** use overshoot or bounce easing. Panels arrive on the default ease.
